title: Goodwill Laredo Central Opens in Former Walgreens on Guadalupe Street
excerpt: Goodwill Laredo Central opened Thursday in a 14,820-square-foot former Walgreens at 1119 Guadalupe Street, the nonprofit's second traditional thrift store in Laredo.
content:
Goodwill Laredo Central opened its doors Thursday, Nov. 12, in a 14,820-square-foot former Walgreens at 1119 Guadalupe Street, giving Laredo shoppers a second traditional Goodwill thrift store.

The new store opened at 10 a.m., according to The Sun, which first reported the opening. It sits just down the street from Goodwill's existing buy-the-pound outlet on Conly Road — but unlike the outlet, the Guadalupe Street shop offers a traditional thrift-store shopping experience, with items priced individually on the racks.

Goodwill's original traditional Laredo store opened on San Dario Avenue in February 2006, meaning the nonprofit has now served Laredo bargain hunters from a traditional storefront for more than 20 years.

Why it matters

Thrift stores do double duty in a border city where household budgets are tight and the secondhand trade is a major local industry. Laredo is home to dozens of textile sorting warehouses that buy, sort and resell used clothing from across the country — and Goodwill stores are a familiar first stop for families looking for affordable clothing, housewares and furniture.

Goodwill says revenue from its stores funds job training and employment services. A new, larger storefront on Guadalupe Street also brings a vacant big-box space back into use on one of the city's older commercial corridors.

Webb Watch 956 could not independently confirm opening-day turnout. The store is open now at 1119 Guadalupe Street.
